newsitem.title: USA: Maine senator repeats plea to O'Leary on heat oil.
newsitem.headline: Maine senator repeats plea to O'Leary on heat oil.

text.p: U.S. Senator Olympia Snowe, Maine Republican, Wednesday pressed Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary to explain why heating oil prices were high and why product was moving to Europe, depleting U.S. stocks.
"Maine experiences harsh winters and its residents are highly dependent on home heating oil, and are particularly hard hit by price increases," Snowe said.

Maine's state planning office estimated that oil prices were about 23 cents per gallon higher than a year ago, which meant consumers would pay $230 more this winter than they did last winter, Snowe said in a letter to O'Leary.
Snowe was among 40 senators and congressmen who wrote to O'Leary last month urging her to find ways to shield consumers from a price spike this winter.
"Since we sent that letter, it appears that the situation has become even more serious," Snowe said.
O'Leary said Wednesday she planned to respond to the lawmakers' concerns before October 18.
